name: a library without roles lets every device do everything
note: Until someone assigns the first role, a library works as before roles existed.

name: an editor adds to the catalog, a reader's addition becomes a request
an editor deletes what her person created, and asks to delete the rest
note: D45. 'Created' means the create change came from a device of the same person, whichever device it was.

name: only an administrator changes roles
an administrator promotes a reader to editor and lets him share
a demotion counts from its moment, whatever the order things arrive in
note: Laura's phone was offline and never saw the demotion. Her change from before it stands; the one after it becomes a request. Every delivery order must end the same, so a device that receives the demotion late re-evaluates the library from its log.

name: a device that belongs to no person acts as a reader
An unsigned operation is refused, with or without roles
note: D56: every operation is signed. 'unsigned' marks an operation without a signature; every other operation here is assumed correctly signed by the device in its hlc. A refused operation is not stored: it is neither applied nor a request.

name: an operation is all or nothing
note: The phone may edit Tersoal's tag but not delete it, so neither change is applied: the whole operation becomes one request.

name: a device renames itself, but only an administrator says whose it is
only an administrator resolves a request, and accepting applies it
note: Hugo, a reader, asks to add a publisher. Laura, an editor, cannot reject it: her attempt becomes a request too. Tersoal, the administrator, accepts it in an operation that also makes the change, signed by him.

name: whoever asked withdraws a request, and nobody else does
note: Hugo, a reader, asks to add a publisher with a note, carried as a change_request row inside the request. Laura, an editor, cannot withdraw Hugo's request: her attempt becomes a request. Hugo withdraws it himself.

name: each person keeps their own marks, whatever their role, and only theirs
note: A reader marks what he read and an editor what she is reading without asking. Changing someone else's mark is for administrators; a device of nobody marks nothing.

name: an operation dated inside the window of a fence becomes a request
note: Laura's phone signs an edit dated between the last operation the administrator had (trusted_through) and the demotion that carries the mark, chained to it. Whatever the order, it is a request: the HLC is the author's word, the fence is the administrator's (D84, D87).

name: an operation dated before the mark of a fence stays applied
note: Everything up to the mark was known to the administrator when the person was demoted, so the fence does not touch it, even if it arrives afterwards.

name: an operation dated below the mark and chained to an older one is a request (SEG-018)
note: Laura is demoted and the fence names her latest operation the administrator had. With a modified app her phone signs a new edit dated below that operation and chained to an older one of hers: a fork. It is not the marked operation nor one of its ancestors, so in any order it is a request. The edit made before the mark and the marked one stay applied.

name: after a fence the person is a reader and the fence changes nothing about that
note: Laura's edit after the demotion is a request, as it is without fences; her edit before it stays applied.

name: a fence set by someone who is not an administrator is ignored
note: Laura (editor) writes a fence on Hugo's tablet. Only administrators touch another device, so her operation is a request and the fence does not count: Hugo's edit dated inside that window stays applied, in every order.

name: a second fence does not reopen the window of the first
note: Laura is demoted, promoted again and demoted again. The device keeps only its latest trusted_through, but the first window comes from the log: the edit dated inside it stays a request.

name: a revoked device writes nothing after its revocation, even without roles
note: D71, D84 (SEG-015): what the device signs after a revocation still in force becomes a request, whichever device passes it on and in whatever order it arrives. What it signed before stays.
